hooks.text: A dead star is slowly vaporizing its own companion into thin air.
Every 1.6 milliseconds, this star pulses while killing its solar partner.
The companion star didn't just explode; it is being eaten alive.

title: The Dead Star That Is Eating Its Companion
description: Astronomers discovered a cannibalistic pulsar that slowly destroys its own partner star through a relentless beam of high-energy radiation.

beats.text: In 1988, astronomers discovered PSR B1957+20, a rapidly spinning neutron star in our galaxy.
beats.visual: Palomar Observatory Samuel Oschin Telescope dome, 1948

beats.text: It rotates once every 1.6 milliseconds, while its small companion completes a tight orbit every 9.2 hours.
beats.visual: Diagram of millisecond pulsar binary Roche lobe accretion and ablation

beats.text: As the pulsar races through space at one million kilometers per hour, it generates a bright bow shock.
beats.visual: Artist concept illustration of the bow shock created by PSR B1957+20

beats.text: The pulsar blasts this partner with radiation, stripping away its surface material until the star becomes nothing.
Fermi data confirms this 1.8 solar mass beast grew by consuming its partner's material.
This is exactly why you will find a dead star is slowly vaporizing its own companion into thin air.
beats.visual: Artist impression of a black widow pulsar evaporating its companion star, 2012

better_than_last: I updated beat 6 to precisely incorporate the reviewer's requested Fermi data phrasing about how the pulsar grew by consuming its partner's material.
